content.value_statement: FluidSim setup can be difficult when solver choices, parameters, and outputs are scattered across docs. This skill turns CFD goals into practical workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation choices for FluidSim with FFT and MPI support.
Selects solvers for Navier-Stokes, stratified flows, shallow water, and elastic plate equations.
Builds parameter plans for domains, viscosity, forcing, time stepping, and outputs.
Drafts workflows for running, restarting, and analyzing simulations.
Explains analysis of physical fields, spectra, spatial means, and HDF5 outputs.
Supports MPI and cluster workflow examples for larger simulations.
limitations: It does not validate the physical model or numerical accuracy.
It requires a local FluidSim installation and compatible scientific libraries.
It assumes periodic domains and equations supported by FluidSim.
Large simulations still need adequate compute resources and storage.

use_cases.title: Prototype A Turbulence Study
use_cases.description: Choose a solver, set resolution and viscosity, and plan saved outputs for a 2D turbulence run.

use_cases.title: Prepare HPC Simulation Runs
use_cases.description: Plan MPI settings, cluster submission scripts, and output directories for high-resolution simulations.

use_cases.title: Teach CFD Workflows
use_cases.description: Explain the standard FluidSim workflow from parameters through execution and result inspection.

prompt_templates.title: Choose A Solver
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a FluidSim solver for a 2D vortex simulation. Explain the main parameters I should set first.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a FluidSim setup plan for a stratified flow simulation with saved physical fields and spectra.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a parametric FluidSim study that varies viscosity and resolution. Include output organization and analysis steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review HPC Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned 3D FluidSim MPI run for solver choice, memory risk, output volume, and restart strategy.

output_examples.input: I need a 2D turbulence run with moderate resolution.
output: Recommends the 2D Navier-Stokes solver for vortex dynamics.
Suggests a moderate grid, adaptive time stepping, viscosity, and saved spectra.
Lists analysis steps for energy and enstrophy trends.

output_examples.input: I want to compare several viscosities.
output: Plans a parametric study with separate output folders for each viscosity.
Keeps resolution and forcing consistent across runs.
Summarizes mean energy and final energy for comparison.

output_examples.input: I am preparing a high-resolution 3D run.
output: Checks that MPI, FFT support, storage, and restart outputs are planned.
Recommends testing the setup at lower resolution before the full run.
Highlights output frequency choices that affect storage use.

best_practices: Start with a low-resolution run before increasing grid size.
Use adaptive time stepping and record the chosen CFL value.
Save enough outputs for restart and analysis without overwhelming storage.
anti_patterns: Starting a large 3D run before validating a smaller case.
Changing viscosity, forcing, and resolution at the same time without a study plan.
Treating default parameters as validated science for every physical problem.

faq.question: Does this skill run FluidSim by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides workflows and examples. The user must run commands in their own environment.

faq.question: Which solvers does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers 2D and 3D Navier-Stokes, stratified flows, shallow water equations, and elastic plate examples.

faq.question: Can it help with MPI runs?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains MPI installation choices, run planning, and cluster workflow patterns.

faq.question: Does it require API keys?
faq.answer: No. The referenced FluidSim workflows do not require API keys or authentication.

faq.question: Can it validate simulation results?
faq.answer: It can suggest validation checks, but it cannot prove a model is physically correct.

faq.question: What outputs can it help analyze?
faq.answer: It covers physical fields, spatial means, spectra, restart files, and parametric study summaries.
